title: Japanese Umbrella Pine: Ancient Japanese Umbrella Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: Not a pine, and the only living species in its family. Old ones at a Hiroshima shrine, a Porto estate and a Bronx cemetery.
intro: Japanese umbrella pine is not a pine at all. It is the only living species in its family, the last of a lineage found in fossils across the northern hemisphere, and it now grows wild only in Japan. What look like needles are flattened green shoots, set in whorls like the ribs of an umbrella. It grows slowly, which is what makes two of ours worth the trip. At Uneyama Shrine in Higashi-Hiroshima, one of the eight trees the prefecture protected as a natural monument in 1987 is 3.2 metres round, and it is still standing after the 1991 typhoon that took several of the grove's trees. In Porto, Portugal's national register measured one on the Quinta de Villar d'Allen at 3.15 metres round and 20 metres tall in 2021 and gave it 151 years, an estimate rather than a planting date. The third stands at a crossroads in Woodlawn Cemetery in the Bronx, one of New York's Great Trees since 1985, with no measurement anyone can trust.
